# Mission Planner Outline

As stated in MissionPlanner\README.md, the Mission Planner teaches users how advanced permanent launch infrastructure, and catch infrastructure, enable interplanetary development, by showing them how such transport would really work, and what its advantages are.

The user first finds viable interplanetary trajectories using the Ephemeris tab. It is designed for quick, easy search for trajectories that successfully arrive at a destination, through patched conic trajectory computation. The user gets a good estimate of the flight's delta v budget, duration, and compatibility with launch and catch infrastructure. Once the user has chosen a flight plan, they can promote it to a mission. 

## Steps to designing a flight in the Ephemeris tab

* As soon as speeds exist in the vector editor shown at right, trajectories are drawn in bright blue in the solar system sim at left. Experimenting with  speeds on different axes shows how that changes the drawn trajectory.

* Pick an origin, and a destination from the drop down lists, which include all the planets, the moon, and several dwarf planets and asteroids.

* In the solar system render, rings are drawn around the selections, showing the equator of each body.

* In the default Solar System view, set the prograde speed at departure via the sidebar vector editor gizmo. Drag along the prograde axis until the trajectory crosses the orbit of the destination.

---

![](data:image/png;base64,)

*Shown in above image:*

* *The departure card vector editor, with values on the prograde and normal axes. It has been zoomed in part way to make drag adjustments easier - there are several more zoom levels available.*

* *The readout box drawn to the left of the vector editor once a vector exists. It converts the speed along the three axes into the speed on the net heading, and in the prograde direction, and the plane change that would result. These values are for the ship as it leaves the SOI of the origin.*

* *The arrows drawn at the origin in the solar system sim show the heading and prograde vector, scaled to show their relative magnitude*

* *Here, the tilt of the Earth's equator reveals that the Earth is poorly aligned to launch in the direction of the vector using infrastructure - something for the user to consider*

* *An orange proximity ring showing where the trajectory crosses the orbit of Psyche, in the top right of the solar system sim*

---

* Next step is to scrub the timelines at the top of the tab, noting when and where proximity rings appear. 

  * Adjusting v_inf on the normal axis can assist in creating crossings

* Click the trajectory to place a chevron on it

  * This causes an X to be drawn where the destination would be when the ship has been flying for the time it takes to reach that point

  * The marker card then displays important data about the trajectory
